articles.title: A Greener City, a Better Life
articles.subtitle: 城市的绿色空间，如何改变日常生活？
articles.provenance: AI 原创示例 · 2026-10-10 · 学习用途，非官方真题

paragraphs.english: As cities expand, a growing population puts pressure on land, housing and transport. Urban planners often face a difficult choice: should an empty site become another office building or a public park? A park may appear less profitable, yet its contribution to residents' well-being can be considerable. Green spaces offer a place to exercise, meet neighbours and escape the noise of crowded streets. For people living in small flats, access to a nearby garden can make everyday life more pleasant.
paragraphs.chinese: 随着城市扩张，人口增长给土地、住房和交通带来压力。城市规划者常常面临选择：空地应该建办公楼还是公园？公园看似利润较低，却能明显改善居民的身心状态。对住在小公寓里的人来说，附近的花园能让生活更加舒适。

paragraphs.english: Trees also play a practical role. Their shade can reduce the heat people experience on a summer afternoon, while soil allows some rainfall to soak into the ground. A sustainable design considers these benefits alongside maintenance costs. However, planting a few trees is not a complete solution to pollution or flooding. Effective policy needs evidence, careful planning and long-term investment. Local authorities should assess each neighbourhood rather than assume that one design will work everywhere.
paragraphs.chinese: 树木也发挥着实际作用。树荫能减轻夏日下午的炎热，土壤则让一部分雨水渗入地下。可持续设计要兼顾这些益处与维护成本，但种几棵树不能彻底解决污染或洪涝问题。有效政策需要证据、细致规划和长期投入，并评估各个社区的实际情况。

paragraphs.english: Another concern is inequality. Wealthier districts may enjoy attractive parks, whereas disadvantaged communities have fewer safe places to relax. To promote fair access, a city could prioritise areas with limited facilities and involve residents in decisions. This approach helps preserve local knowledge and builds a sense of responsibility. Ultimately, a successful green project is not measured only by the number of trees planted. It should improve the environment while responding to the needs of the people who use it.
paragraphs.chinese: 另一个问题是资源不平等。较富裕的地区可能拥有漂亮的公园，而弱势社区缺少安全的休闲场所。城市可以优先改善设施不足的地区，并让居民参与决策。成功的绿化项目不只看种了多少树，还要改善环境并回应使用者的需求。

articles.title: Learning Beyond the Classroom
articles.subtitle: 技能会变化，学习也不必止于毕业。
articles.provenance: AI 原创示例 · 2026-10-10 · 学习用途，非官方真题

paragraphs.english: For many people, education once meant attending school and obtaining a qualification before entering employment. Today, technological change can alter the skills a job requires within a few years. An employee who could previously rely on familiar methods may need to adapt to new software or work with colleagues in different countries. Lifelong learning offers a way to respond to this uncertainty. It does not always require a university degree: a short course, a practical workshop or guided practice can also be useful.
paragraphs.chinese: 对许多人来说，教育曾意味着上学、获得资格，然后就业。如今，技术变化可能在几年内改变一份工作所需的技能。终身学习能帮助人们应对这种不确定性，也不一定意味着攻读大学学位：短期课程、实践工作坊或有指导的练习同样有用。

paragraphs.english: Online courses provide flexibility, especially for adults balancing work and family responsibilities. Learners can choose a convenient time and repeat difficult lessons. Nevertheless, convenience alone does not guarantee progress. Motivation often declines when a course feels disconnected from real life. To acquire a skill effectively, learners need clear goals, regular feedback and opportunities to apply what they have studied. A person learning to write reports, for instance, might practise with a realistic task instead of simply watching more videos.
paragraphs.chinese: 在线课程为兼顾工作与家庭的成年人提供了灵活性，但便利本身不能保证进步。当课程与现实脱节时，学习动力往往会下降。有效掌握技能需要明确目标、定期反馈和实践机会。例如，学习报告写作的人可以练习真实任务，而不只是不断观看视频。

paragraphs.english: Employers have a role as well. If training is available only outside working hours, some staff may struggle to participate. Organisations can allocate time for learning and encourage experienced workers to share expertise. Such support may strengthen confidence and help a team solve unfamiliar problems. However, responsibility should not fall entirely on individuals or businesses. Public libraries and community centres can offer affordable resources, making learning more inclusive. The broader aim is not merely to increase productivity, but to enable people to make informed choices throughout their lives.
paragraphs.chinese: 雇主也有责任。如果培训只能在下班后进行，一些员工可能难以参加。组织可以安排学习时间，鼓励经验丰富的员工分享专业知识。图书馆和社区中心也可提供价格合理的资源，让学习更包容。学习的目标不仅是提高生产效率，也包括帮助人们一生中作出知情的选择。

questions.explanation: 第一段列出短期课程、工作坊和有指导的练习，表明终身学习有多种形式。

questions.prompt: Why might motivation decline in an online course?
options: The course seems disconnected from real life.

questions.explanation: 第二段指出课程与现实脱节时，学习动力往往会下降。

questions.explanation: 第三段建议组织分配学习时间，并支持员工分享专业知识。

articles.title: The Value of Our Attention
articles.subtitle: 在数字生活中，为专注留一点空间。
articles.provenance: AI 原创示例 · 2026-10-10 · 学习用途，非官方真题

paragraphs.english: Digital devices have transformed the way people communicate and obtain information. A message can reach a friend in seconds, and a student can explore a vast range of learning materials without leaving home. Yet the same devices may interrupt activities that require concentration. Notifications compete for attention, encouraging users to switch between a task and a screen. The issue is not simply how much time people spend online, but whether their habits support the activities they consider important.
paragraphs.chinese: 数字设备改变了人们沟通和获取信息的方式，却也可能打断需要专注的活动。通知争夺注意力，促使用户在任务和屏幕之间切换。问题不只是花了多少时间上网，还包括使用习惯是否支持自己真正重视的事情。

paragraphs.english: One possible strategy is to establish boundaries. Someone working on a demanding assignment could silence unnecessary alerts and set aside a period for checking messages. This approach aims to minimise distraction while preserving the benefits of communication. It is also useful to evaluate which applications deserve frequent use. An application that helps a person maintain relationships serves a different purpose from one opened automatically whenever there is a spare moment. Recognising that distinction can make decisions more deliberate.
paragraphs.chinese: 一种策略是建立界限。处理复杂任务时，可以关闭不必要的提醒，并安排专门时间查看消息。这样既能减少干扰，又能保留沟通的好处。我们也可以评估哪些应用值得频繁使用，区分主动维护关系与空闲时下意识打开应用，让选择更加有意识。

paragraphs.english: Personal habits, however, are only part of the picture. Designers can influence behaviour through default settings and the way information is presented. A service that offers clear controls may help users manage their experience, whereas a confusing interface can make that harder. Greater transparency about recommendations could support informed choices. There is no single routine that suits everyone: a parent, a student and a shift worker have different needs. A balanced relationship with technology therefore depends on both thoughtful design and individual reflection, rather than on the assumption that every digital activity is harmful.
paragraphs.chinese: 个人习惯只是问题的一部分。设计者也会通过默认设置和信息呈现方式影响行为。清晰的控制选项与推荐机制透明度有助于用户作出知情的选择。适合每个人的统一日程并不存在，因此平衡的数字生活需要良好设计与个人反思。

vocabulary.example: Online tools have transformed the way teams collaborate.
Reading a complex argument requires concentration.
Planning breaks can be an effective strategy.
Families can establish clear boundaries for device use.
A quiet workspace helps minimise distraction.
Turning off alerts may reduce distraction.
Users should evaluate the benefits of each tool.
There is a distinction between useful breaks and constant interruption.

options: Whether habits support important activities.

questions.explanation: 第一段强调，应考虑数字使用习惯是否支持自己重视的活动，而不只计算上网时间。

questions.prompt: Which action is suggested to minimise distraction?
options: Check every notification immediately.
Silence unnecessary alerts during demanding work.

questions.explanation: 第二段建议在复杂任务期间关闭不必要的提醒，同时安排时间处理消息。

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the final paragraph?
options: Every person should follow the same routine.
All digital activity is harmful.

questions.explanation: 最后一段说明，个人需求不同，平衡的数字生活取决于良好设计与个人反思。

articles.provenance: AI 原创分级练习 · 2026-10-10 · 同主题情境加分级论述段；难度未作教学标定

paragraphs.english: The following scenario illustrates how practical decisions involve competing needs. Its value lies not in a universal solution, but in the questions it invites readers to examine. Three students meet after class to review a difficult lesson. Each person explains one idea in their own words. When an explanation is unclear, the others ask for an example. The group tries to understand the lesson rather than copy one person's notes. A question that seems simple can reveal a gap in understanding and give everyone a useful reason to think again.
paragraphs.chinese: 下面的情境展示实际决策如何涉及不同需求。其价值在于引导思考问题，而不是提供通用答案。三位学生课后复习，每人用自己的话解释一个概念，不清楚时就请对方举例。目标是理解，而不是抄笔记。简单问题也可能暴露理解中的空缺。

paragraphs.english: The students agree on a purpose for each meeting and divide the tasks fairly. They check an answer against the course material instead of assuming that the most confident speaker is right. Cooperation can make study more active, but it does not remove the need for individual practice. A group also needs to notice when one person does all the work and others remain silent.
paragraphs.chinese: 大家约定目标、公平分工，并对照教材核实答案，不盲从最自信的人。合作不能取代个人练习，也要留意是否有人承担全部工作、其他人一直沉默。

paragraphs.english: An effective approach needs evidence about the people it is intended to help. A change can have a significant impact without solving every problem, and limited resources make priorities unavoidable. Investment should therefore be assessed alongside the effort required to maintain a service or habit. A sustainable solution is one that can continue under realistic conditions, rather than one that looks attractive only at the beginning. Asking who benefits, what remains uncertain and how progress will be checked can make the discussion more precise. Those questions connect a promising idea with the circumstances in which it must work.
paragraphs.chinese: 有效方法需要了解服务对象的证据。改变可能产生显著影响，却无法解决全部问题；资源有限，必须确定优先事项。投入要与持续维护的成本一起评估。可持续方案应能在现实条件下继续运行。追问谁受益、仍有哪些不确定性、如何检查进展，可以让讨论更准确。

paragraphs.english: An apparently straightforward intervention can conceal questions about agency, distribution and accountability. The scenario below provides a concrete starting point from which to examine those tensions. Three students meet after class to review a difficult lesson. Each person explains one idea in their own words. When an explanation is unclear, the others ask for an example. The group tries to understand the lesson rather than copy one person's notes. A question that seems simple can reveal a gap in understanding and give everyone a useful reason to think again.
paragraphs.chinese: 看似直接的干预也可能掩盖主体作用、分配和责任等问题。下面的情境提供了分析这些张力的具体起点。三位学生课后复习，每人用自己的话解释一个概念，不清楚时就请对方举例。目标是理解，而不是抄笔记。简单问题也可能暴露理解中的空缺。

paragraphs.english: The students agree on a purpose for each meeting and divide the tasks fairly. They check an answer against the course material instead of assuming that the most confident speaker is right. Cooperation can make study more active, but it does not remove the need for individual practice. A group also needs to notice when one person does all the work and others remain silent.
paragraphs.chinese: 大家约定目标、公平分工，并对照教材核实答案，不盲从最自信的人。合作不能取代个人练习，也要留意是否有人承担全部工作、其他人一直沉默。

paragraphs.english: A credible framework should make its central assumption explicit rather than treating it as a neutral fact. The implications of a decision depend partly on the incentives faced by the people involved and the constraints under which they act. An equitable outcome therefore cannot be inferred from a favourable average alone. Proposals warrant scrutiny when their apparent benefits conceal a trade-off between convenience and participation. This does not imply that improvement is impossible; it means that the reasoning must identify who gains, who carries the burden and which alternatives were excluded. Evaluating those questions is more informative than accepting a single indicator as definitive proof of success.
paragraphs.chinese: 可信的框架应明确核心假设，而不是把假设当成中性事实。决策的影响取决于参与者面对的激励和限制。仅凭较好的平均值不能推断结果公平。若表面益处掩盖了便利与参与之间的取舍，方案应接受审视。这并非否定改进，而是要求论证说明谁获益、谁承担负担、哪些替代方案被排除。

paragraphs.english: This story begins with an ordinary situation. The people involved want to make daily life a little easier. A teacher returns a student's short essay with several comments. At first, the student looks only at the mark. Later, she reads the comments and notices that her main argument is difficult to follow. She asks the teacher to identify one paragraph that needs attention. A specific example helps her understand the difference between an interesting idea and a clear explanation.
paragraphs.chinese: 故事从一个日常场景开始，其中的人想让生活变得更轻松。老师退回作文后，学生最初只看分数，后来才发现评语指出主要论证不够清晰。她请老师选出一个需要修改的段落，借具体例子理解如何清楚解释观点。

paragraphs.english: The student rewrites the paragraph and compares the two versions. She keeps the part that already works and changes the sentences that confuse the reader. Feedback becomes useful when there is an opportunity to act on it. Nevertheless, too many comments at once can be overwhelming. A manageable goal may help more than a long list of faults without any explanation of what to do next.
paragraphs.chinese: 学生重写段落、比较两个版本，保留优点并修改造成困惑的句子。反馈需要行动机会才有价值；一次评论过多也会令人负担沉重，目标应当可执行。

paragraphs.english: When people choose what to do, they need a clear plan. A small step can bring a benefit. It is useful to share an idea and ask a question. People can learn from a mistake. They can also change a plan when it does not work. The aim is not to do everything in one day. The aim is to find a way that fits real life. It helps to talk about what went well and what was hard. This makes the next choice easier.
paragraphs.chinese: 决定做什么时，人们需要明确计划。小步骤也能带来益处。分享想法、提出问题、从错误中学习，都能帮助行动。计划无效时可以调整；目标不是一天完成所有事情，而是找到适合现实生活的做法，回顾顺利和困难之处，让下次选择更容易。

paragraphs.english: This story begins with an ordinary situation. The people involved want to make daily life a little easier. They notice a narrow junction where drivers often turn quickly. Rather than drawing only a continuous line on a map, the team asks how a cyclist would cross this point safely and where a bicycle could be parked at the end.

paragraphs.english: The town tests a temporary layout and collects comments from pedestrians as well as cyclists. Connectivity matters because a comfortable section is less useful when the next section is difficult to reach. The team also considers maintenance after heavy rain. This makes the next choice easier.

paragraphs.english: The following scenario illustrates how practical decisions involve competing needs. Its value lies not in a universal solution, but in the questions it invites readers to examine. The village invites walkers and conservation volunteers to discuss a clearer route. They compare possible signs and consider whether a viewing area could allow people to enjoy the coast without entering a sensitive section of the shore.

paragraphs.english: The group checks how access changes with the season and asks volunteers to record what they observe. Those questions connect a promising idea with the circumstances in which it must work.

paragraphs.english: This story begins with an ordinary situation. The people involved want to make daily life a little easier. People living near a busy square discuss noise from evening deliveries. paragraphs.english: This story begins with an ordinary situation. The people involved want to make daily life a little easier. A learner draws a diagram after reading a chapter about cities. She places the main idea in the centre and connects it to examples from the text. When she tries to explain a connection aloud, she discovers that one arrow has no clear meaning. She returns to the chapter and revises the diagram. The drawing becomes a way to ask questions rather than merely a colourful record of familiar words.
paragraphs.chinese: 故事从一个日常场景开始，其中的人想让生活变得更轻松。学习者读完城市主题章节后画图，把中心概念与文中例子相连。尝试口头解释时，她发现一个箭头没有明确含义，便回到原文修改。图示于是成为提问工具，而不只是熟悉词语的彩色记录。

paragraphs.english: Her study partner makes a different diagram and explains why an example belongs in another position. Comparing the diagrams reveals a gap in each person's understanding. A visual representation may support explanation, but it does not replace reading the original argument carefully. A tidy diagram can still contain a mistaken relationship. The pair therefore checks its links against the text and keeps notes on questions that remain unresolved.
paragraphs.chinese: 同伴画出不同图示，并解释为何把一个例子放在别处。比较暴露了两人的理解缺口。视觉表达可以辅助解释，却不能代替仔细阅读论证。整洁图表仍可能包含错误关系，所以两人核对原文，并记录尚未解决的问题。

paragraphs.english: When people choose what to do, they need a clear plan. A small step can bring a benefit. It is useful to share an idea and ask a question. People can learn from a mistake. They can also change a plan when it does not work. The aim is not to do everything in one day. The aim is to find a way that fits real life. It helps to talk about what went well and what was hard. This makes the next choice easier.
paragraphs.chinese: 决定做什么时，人们需要明确计划。小步骤也能带来益处。分享想法、提出问题、从错误中学习，都能帮助行动。计划无效时可以调整；目标不是一天完成所有事情，而是找到适合现实生活的做法，回顾顺利和困难之处，让下次选择更容易。

The pair therefore checks its links against the text and keeps notes on questions that remain unresolved.

paragraphs.english: A credible framework should make its central assumption explicit rather than treating it as a neutral fact. The implications of a decision depend partly on the incentives faced by the people involved and the constraints under which they act. Evaluating those questions is more informative than accepting a single indicator as definitive proof of success.

paragraphs.english: This story begins with an ordinary situation. The people involved want to make daily life a little easier. A student creates a revision plan for an upcoming examination. She begins with a short practice task and records which errors she makes. Instead of spending equal time on every chapter, she gives more attention to topics that she cannot yet explain. She also leaves time to revisit earlier material. The plan is a working guide that can change when practice shows a different pattern of strengths and difficulties.

paragraphs.english: After a week, she checks whether her practice resembles the tasks she will face. Memorising a model response may feel reassuring, but a question with a different focus can require a different answer. paragraphs.english: This story begins with an ordinary situation. The people involved want to make daily life a little easier. A community joins a project that records plants in local streets. A researcher provides a protocol describing when to observe, what to photograph and how to note an uncertain identification. Participants practise together before submitting a record. Their familiarity with the area can help them notice changes, but shared instructions are also needed if observations from different people are to be compared in a useful way.

paragraphs.english: The project includes a review stage where a specialist checks records that require more attention. A dataset may contain gaps because participants cannot visit every street at every time. The researcher explains those limits when presenting results and avoids describing unrecorded locations as places without plants. Public participation can add valuable observations, while careful interpretation still depends on understanding how the records were collected and which places were left out.
paragraphs.chinese: 项目安排专家复查需要关注的记录。参与者无法随时走访每条街，因此数据可能有缺口。研究者呈现结果时解释限制，不把未记录地点描述为没有植物。公众参与能提供有价值的观察，而解释仍需了解采集方式及遗漏地点。

paragraphs.english: When people choose what to do, they need a clear plan. A small step can bring a benefit. It is useful to share an idea and ask a question. People can learn from a mistake. This makes the next choice easier.
paragraphs.chinese: 决定做什么时，人们需要明确计划。小步骤也能带来益处。分享想法、提出问题、从错误中学习，都能帮助行动。计划无效时可以调整；目标不是一天完成所有事情，而是找到适合现实生活的做法，回顾顺利和困难之处，让下次选择更容易。

paragraphs.english: An apparently straightforward intervention can conceal questions about agency, distribution and accountability. The scenario below provides a concrete starting point from which to examine those tensions. A community joins a project that records plants in local streets. A researcher provides a protocol describing when to observe, what to photograph and how to note an uncertain identification. Participants practise together before submitting a record. Their familiarity with the area can help them notice changes, but shared instructions are also needed if observations from different people are to be compared in a useful way.

paragraphs.english: The project includes a review stage where a specialist checks records that require more attention. A dataset may contain gaps because participants cannot visit every street at every time. paragraphs.chinese: 项目安排专家复查需要关注的记录。参与者无法随时走访每条街，因此数据可能有缺口。研究者呈现结果时解释限制，不把未记录地点描述为没有植物。公众参与能提供有价值的观察，而解释仍需了解采集方式及遗漏地点。

paragraphs.english: A credible framework should make its central assumption explicit rather than treating it as a neutral fact. The implications of a decision depend partly on the incentives faced by the people involved and the constraints under which they act. This does not imply that improvement is impossible; it means that the reasoning must identify who gains, who carries the burden and which alternatives were excluded. Evaluating those questions is more informative than accepting a single indicator as definitive proof of success.

paragraphs.english: This story begins with an ordinary situation. The people involved want to make daily life a little easier. A training provider uses an automated system to help organise applications. The system gives each application a score based on the information supplied. A member of staff asks which criterion contributes to that score and whether missing information is treated differently from a low result. The provider wants to understand the process before relying on its output. A number can look precise without explaining how a particular person was assessed.
paragraphs.chinese: 故事从一个日常场景开始，其中的人想让生活变得更轻松。培训机构用自动系统辅助整理申请。系统依据资料评分，员工询问哪些标准影响结果，以及缺失信息是否区别于低成绩处理。机构希望先理解流程再依赖输出，因为一个精确数字未必解释了具体申请者如何被评估。

paragraphs.english: The provider introduces an appeal route and checks examples with staff who understand the course requirements. An audit can identify some patterns, but it cannot by itself decide which outcomes are fair. People may disagree about the criteria or about the evidence an applicant should be able to provide. This makes the next choice easier.

paragraphs.english: This story begins with an ordinary situation. The people involved want to make daily life a little easier. A team meets to discuss a delayed project. paragraphs.english: A small decision can reveal how everyday choices affect other people. Consider the following example, and look for the reason behind each action. A neighbourhood receives a small budget for a shared project. Residents suggest new benches, clearer signs and equipment for a meeting room. The facilitator asks each group to explain who would benefit and what the project would require after it was completed. A proposal becomes easier to compare when its purpose, estimated cost and continuing needs are visible. The discussion includes people who may use the project less often but still contribute to it.
paragraphs.chinese: 一个小决定也可能显示日常选择如何影响他人。阅读下面的例子，思考每个行动背后的原因。社区收到一笔共享项目预算。居民提出长椅、标识和活动室设备等方案。主持者请各组说明谁受益、完成后还需要什么。当目的、估计成本与持续需要都明确时，方案更易比较。讨论也纳入使用较少但仍会参与投入的人。

paragraphs.english: The group publishes its selection criteria and offers a way to submit comments outside the meeting. A vote can show the preferences of those who participate, but it does not automatically represent everyone in the neighbourhood. Some residents may find the process difficult to access. The group therefore reviews participation as well as the final result and explains why the chosen project was prioritised over the alternatives that were proposed.
paragraphs.chinese: 小组公布选择标准，提供会外提交意见的渠道。投票显示参加者的偏好，却不会自动代表所有居民，因为部分人可能难以参与。团队因此同时检查参与过程与结果，并解释所选项目为何优先于其他方案。

paragraphs.english: People can improve a routine when they connect a new idea with experience. Before they begin, they should compare the options available to them. The next step should follow from that record, rather than from a promise of a perfect result.
paragraphs.chinese: 把新想法与经验联系起来，有助于改进日常做法。行动前应比较可选方案。实际计划既考虑时间、资金，也关注结果质量。朋友或老师的支持可以帮助形成习惯，但适合一个人的方案未必适合另一个人。简短记录让进步更容易被发现，也帮助决定下一步。

paragraphs.english: An apparently straightforward intervention can conceal questions about agency, distribution and accountability. The scenario below provides a concrete starting point from which to examine those tensions. A neighbourhood receives a small budget for a shared project. Residents suggest new benches, clearer signs and equipment for a meeting room. The facilitator asks each group to explain who would benefit and what the project would require after it was completed. A proposal becomes easier to compare when its purpose, estimated cost and continuing needs are visible. The discussion includes people who may use the project less often but still contribute to it.
paragraphs.chinese: 看似直接的干预也可能掩盖主体作用、分配和责任等问题。下面的情境提供了分析这些张力的具体起点。社区收到一笔共享项目预算。居民提出长椅、标识和活动室设备等方案。主持者请各组说明谁受益、完成后还需要什么。当目的、估计成本与持续需要都明确时，方案更易比较。讨论也纳入使用较少但仍会参与投入的人。

paragraphs.english: The group publishes its selection criteria and offers a way to submit comments outside the meeting. A vote can show the preferences of those who participate, but it does not automatically represent everyone in the neighbourhood. Some residents may find the process difficult to access. The group therefore reviews participation as well as the final result and explains why the chosen project was prioritised over the alternatives that were proposed.
paragraphs.chinese: 小组公布选择标准，提供会外提交意见的渠道。投票显示参加者的偏好，却不会自动代表所有居民，因为部分人可能难以参与。团队因此同时检查参与过程与结果，并解释所选项目为何优先于其他方案。

paragraphs.english: A credible framework should make its central assumption explicit rather than treating it as a neutral fact. The implications of a decision depend partly on the incentives faced by the people involved and the constraints under which they act. An equitable outcome therefore cannot be inferred from a favourable average alone. Proposals warrant scrutiny when their apparent benefits conceal a trade-off between convenience and participation. This does not imply that improvement is impossible; it means that the reasoning must identify who gains, who carries the burden and which alternatives were excluded. Evaluating those questions is more informative than accepting a single indicator as definitive proof of success.
paragraphs.chinese: 可信的框架应明确核心假设，而不是把假设当成中性事实。决策的影响取决于参与者面对的激励和限制。仅凭较好的平均值不能推断结果公平。若表面益处掩盖了便利与参与之间的取舍，方案应接受审视。这并非否定改进，而是要求论证说明谁获益、谁承担负担、哪些替代方案被排除。
